LINE-SGD would plausibly beat graph factorization on Wikipedia page classification when the graph is weighted and its edge weights are consistent, meaning they reliably reflect true page-to-page similarity (for example, link or co-occurrence strength). Under those conditions, LINE's edge-sampling SGD objective, which models first- and second-order proximity, can exploit the weights directly, while graph factorization of the adjacency matrix is more sensitive to noisy or inconsistent weighting and to scale. The advantage would also depend on the labels being homophilous, so that neighboring pages tend to share a class.
